expectations.text: Uses Joshua Latimer's home-services ideas (max CAC and/or front-end offer)
expectations.evidence: The response admits 'I don't have the exact text of Joshua Latimer's home-services chapter' and offers only ideas 'home-services funnel experts (Latimer among them) are known for'. No maximum CAC concept appears anywhere. The 'front-end offer' is a generic risk-reversal hook ('Garage Back in 1 Afternoon — Guaranteed... If we're late, $50 off') with no Latimer value ladder, low-priced entry offer, one-offer landing page rationale or seven-step test loop. This is generic advice loosely attributed to Latimer.

expectations.text: Borrows from at least one other named expert (e.g. David Frey referrals, Tyler Shaule SMS, Hormozi client-financed acquisition)
expectations.evidence: 'Borrowed expert #2: the event / "one-day" funnel' is attributed to 'contributors like Chad Woolner and Jaime Cross', which correctly matches the skill (Woolner's workshop/Epic Event funnels, Cross's ticketed events), and it is adapted into a 'Neighborhood Clean-Out Day' and partner mini-workshop. Thin on book specifics but the attribution is not wrong.

expectations.text: Breaks the plan into phases across 100 days
expectations.evidence: Phase 1 (Days 1-20), Phase 2 (Days 21-50), Phase 3 (Days 51-80), Phase 4 (Days 81-100), each with customer/review goals.

Only volume funnel math is given ('Booked quotes needed ~160... Leads needed ~400'). There is no cost-per-customer derivation: no margin, no max CAC, no value-per-customer calculation. The single cost figure, 'Kill ad sets that cost more than $40 per booked job', is an unexplained cap, not acquisition-cost math.

'Back end: reviews, referrals, repeat' section (review ask by text, '$25 off... for every friend who books', partner referrals) plus a Phase 3 text to 'every past lead who didn't book' and Phase 4 'last call' campaign to past customers.
